meaning:
1) to wear out, become old
1a) (Qal) to wear out
1b) (Piel)
1b1) to wear out
1b2) to wear out by use, use up completely
1b3) to enjoy, use to the full
Aramaic equivalent: be.la (בְּלָא "to wear out" H1080)

renderings.kjv: all of them shall wax old

elsewhere.note: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
Your clothing didn’t grow old on you, neither did your foot swell, these forty years.
These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.”
I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will…
“Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.
though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
When I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long.
Behold, the Lord Yahweh will help me! Who is he who will condemn me? Behold, they will all grow old like a garment. The moths will eat them up.
